lines: Six winters. One valley of mud.
The Great War ended everywhere else. Here... it never did.
On one side, the Hegemony. Field grey, and iron discipline.
On the other, the Concord. Free men in khaki, who only want to go home.
And between them, a front full of empty posts. Rifles with no names.
Comment your side under our pinned reel, and a soldier takes the line. With your name on it. For good.
Rifleman. Sniper. Stretcher bearer. Every soldier gets a trade, a rank, and a service record, written one day at a time.
Every midnight, the front turns. Men are wounded. Men are promoted. Some don't come back.
But no name dies out. When a soldier falls, the next of the family picks up the rifle.
And every day, you decide what happens next. Hold the line, or go over the top. Vote in the comments.
Five hundred claimed soldiers, and the big guns wake up.
The first hundred recruits wear the First Wave medal. Forever.
